source_text:
Σπίχκε΄. Καὶ κατέστρεφεν τὰς πόλεις ταύτας, καὶ πασαν τὴν περίχωρον, καὶ πάντας τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι.
Στίχ. κς΄. Καὶ ἀπέλεψεν ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω, καὶ ἐγένετο στήλη ἁλός.
Ὁ Κύριος οὐ μόνον τοὺς ἀσεβεῖς ἀπόλλυσιν, ἀλλὰ καὶ τὰς τροφὰς αὐτῶν οὔσας Σοδομιτικὰς καὶ ἐπιβλαβεῖς· ἐν αἷς ἐστι καὶ ἄμπελος, περὶ ἧς γέγραπται· Ἐκ γὰρ ἀμπέλου Σοδόμων ἡ ἄμπελος αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ κλημαεὶς αὐτῶν ἐκ Γομόῤῤας. (5) Ἅμα τε εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπεσώθη, καὶ τὸ πῦρ ἐπεφέρετο ταῖς πόλεσι, σημεῖον τῆς μελλούσης συντελείας. Στήλη οὐχ ἁπλῶς ἐγένετο, ἀλλὰ μάλιστα στήλη ἁλὸς, διὰ τό· Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἄλας τῆς γῆς. Ἐφαρμόσῃ δὲ τῇ στήλῃ τοῦ ἁλὸς τό· Ἐὰν δὲ τὸ ἅλας μωρανθῇ; Οὐκ ἀθρόως ἀναβαίνει εἰς τὸ ὄρος κατὰ τὰ εἰρημένα αὐτῷ, ἀλλὰ πρῶτον εἰς Σηγὼρ γίνεται, καίτοιγε μὴ θαῤῥήσας ἑαυτῷ περὶ τοῦ ἀναβῆναι εἰς τὸ ὄρος.
thought_title: Sodom's destruction and Lot's wife as salt
orientation: Origen is commenting on Genesis 19:25-26, explaining the destruction of Sodom and the meaning of Lot's wife becoming a pillar of salt.
pass_a_gloss: And he was overthrowing these cities, and all the surrounding region, and all those dwelling in the cities. And his wife looked back to the things behind, and she became a pillar of salt. The Lord not only destroys the impious, but also their foods, being Sodomitic and harmful; among which is also the vine, about which it is written: For from the vine of Sodom their vine, and their branch from Gomorrah. At the same time he was brought safely into the city, and the fire was brought upon the cities, a sign of the coming end of the age. A pillar she did not simply become, but especially a pillar of salt, because of: You are the salt of the earth. And will you apply to the pillar of salt the: But if the salt becomes foolish? Not all at once does he go up into the mountain according to the things said to him, but first he comes to Zoar, although indeed not having confidence in himself about going up into the mountain.

choices.why: The imperfect tense conveys ongoing action in the narrative; 'overthrowing' matches the Septuagint's use of this verb for divine destruction of cities.

choices.english: looked back to the things behind
choices.why: The phrase 'εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω' specifies direction; keeping 'to the things behind' preserves the literal force of the prepositional phrase.
The passive voice indicates the fire was brought by divine agency; 'was brought upon' preserves the passive and the prepositional force.
The verb means 'to become foolish' or 'to lose taste'; 'becomes foolish' preserves the literal sense and the connection to salt losing its saltiness.
The dative reflexive pronoun with the participle conveys self-confidence; keeping 'in himself' preserves the reflexive force.

bible_refs.note: Καὶ κατέστρεφεν τὰς πόλεις ταύτας, καὶ πασαν τὴν περίχωρον, καὶ πάντας τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι.
Καὶ ἀπέλεψεν ἡ γυνὴ αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰ ὀπίσω, καὶ ἐγένετο στήλη ἁλός.
Ἐκ γὰρ ἀμπέλου Σοδόμων ἡ ἄμπελος αὐτῶν καὶ ἡ κλημαεὶς αὐτῶν ἐκ Γομόῤῥας.
Ὑμεῖς ἐστε τὸ ἄλας τῆς γῆς.

pass_b_english: He destroyed these cities, the surrounding region, and all who dwelt in them, and the Lord destroys not only the impious but also their foods, which are Sodomitic and harmful. Among these is the vine, about which it is written: “For their vine is from the vine of Sodom, and their branch from Gomorrah” (Deuteronomy 32:32). At the same time he was rescued into the city, and the fire was brought upon the cities as a sign of the coming end of the age. She did not become just any pillar, but specifically a pillar of salt, because of the words: “You are the salt of the earth” (Matthew 5:13). And does not the saying “But if the salt becomes foolish” (Matthew 5:13) apply to the pillar of salt? He does not go up into the mountain all at once according to what was told him, but first goes to Zoar, even though he had no confidence in himself about going up into the mountain.
notes: The lemma form 'κλημαεὶς' appears to be a variant or misspelling of 'κληματίς' (branch); the text as transmitted reads 'κλημαεὶς'.

problems.quote: The Lord destroys not only the impious but also their foods, which are Sodomitic and harmful.
problems.source_quote: Καὶ κατέστρεφεν τὰς πόλεις ταύτας, καὶ πασαν τὴν περίχωρον, καὶ πάντας τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι.
problems.why: The English skips the clause that the Lord destroyed the cities, the surrounding area, and all inhabitants.
problems.fix: He destroyed these cities, the surrounding region, and all who dwelt in them, and also destroyed the impious and their foods, which are Sodomitic and harmful.

problems.quote: Lot was brought safely into the city
problems.why: Source is impersonal passive 'he was saved/rescued to the city'; English adds 'Lot' and 'brought' (agency change).
problems.fix: he was rescued into the city
problems.ruling: Source says simply “he was saved into the city” (εἰς τὴν πόλιν ἀπεσώθη); English adds “Lot” and “brought”, changing subject and agency.

edits.old: The Lord destroys not only the impious but also their foods, which are Sodomitic and harmful.
edits.new: He destroyed these cities, the surrounding region, and all who dwelt in them, and the Lord destroys not only the impious but also their foods, which are Sodomitic and harmful.

edits.old: At the same time that Lot was brought safely into the city, the fire was brought upon the cities
edits.new: At the same time he was rescued into the city, and the fire was brought upon the cities

fixed: Added the omitted clause about destroying the cities, surrounding region, and inhabitants, matching the source Καὶ κατέστρεφεν τὰς πόλεις ταύτας, καὶ πασαν τὴν περίχωρον, καὶ πάντας τοὺς κατοικοῦντας ἐν ταῖς πόλεσι.
Changed 'Lot was brought safely into the city' to 'he was rescued into the city' to match the impersonal passive ἀπεσώθη without adding 'Lot' or implying an agent.

last_rejected.quote: he was rescued into the city
last_rejected.why: ἀπεσώθη is 3rd person singular; context is Lot being rescued to Zoar, not 'he' (the Lord).
last_rejected.fix: Lot was rescued to the city
last_rejected.ruling: Greek ἀπεσώθη = ‘was rescued’; English ‘he was rescued’ matches; pronoun reference unclear but not a mistranslation of the verb

last_rejected.quote: And does not the saying “But if the salt becomes foolish” (Matthew 5:13) apply to the pillar of salt?
last_rejected.source_quote: Ἐφαρμόσῃ δὲ τῇ στήλῃ τοῦ ἁλὸς
last_rejected.why: Greek adds a rhetorical question about applying the salt to the pillar of salt, which is omitted in English.
last_rejected.fix: Add a sentence such as: “And should we not apply the salt to the pillar of salt?” before the question about the foolish salt.
last_rejected.ruling: English 'And does not the saying...apply to the pillar of salt?' renders Ἐφαρμόσῃ δὲ τῇ στήλῃ τοῦ ἁλὸς; nothing omitted.
